newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures trade down in more active market.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures trade down in more active market.

text.p: Sydney wheat futures turned more active on Wednesday with 24 contracts selling in a falling near-term market which stayed firm in more distant contracts.
July, September, November 1997 and January 1998 all traded, falling by a range of 50 cents to A$5.50 on the trades.
Nearby July 1997 showed the biggest fall, A$5.50 a tonne to A$200.00, while the most heavily-traded contract January 1998 fell by A$1.50 on the trade to A$176.00.
However, most settlement prices edged up, mostly by 50 cents, with distant September 1998 improving by A$3.00.
Chris Gray of C, A & L Bell Commodities Corp said January 1998 had found a level most traders were happy with.
Some farmer selling entered the market after last night's Chicago decline. Most sales in the January contract were in dribs and drabs with three lots the biggest trade.
A tight cash market continues to influence the front months, he said. Australian weather were not a major influence with growers still needing rain for back-month contracts.
More optimistic U.S. weather was having a greater effect, but Chicago's soybean fall was the greatest influence, he said.
